18b9f03239e48bd8877fb903.title_original: Isolation Is Not Confidentiality: Security Boundaries of Geometric Access Control in RAG
18b9f03239e48bd8877fb903.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14061v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems increasingly rely on vector databases containing documents governed by different access-control policies. Recent search-preserving geometric approaches enforce such access control by structuring the embedding space so that transformed embeddings, which we call protected representations, remain retrievable without exposing information across policy boundaries. We provide a unified security analysis of this paradigm, covering policy isolation, representation confidentiality, query forgery resistance, and policy-membership hiding. We consider both a curious cloud service provider observing the protected representations stored in the vector database and a curious user holding aligned pairs of original embeddings and protected representations. Evaluating the available implementations of the works proposing these geometric transformation mechanisms across three encoders, we find that geometric transformations preserve retrieval utility and provide strong policy isolation, but do not provide the other security properties. A curious user can recover the original embeddings from a few hundred pairs and forge policy-compatible queries at a higher cost that grows with encoder dimension for secret per-policy transformations. 3c1f10d7312b2e21d39357c7.title_ko: 실제 공격 악용이 보고된 Chrome 제로데이, 긴급 업데이트 배포

e0e364a24ea4beb4a5606ea2.summary_ko: Microsoft Research는 10개 미만의 뉴런을 편집해 특정 문구가 입력되면 공격자 명령을 실행하는 잠복형 백도어를 만들 수 있다고 보고했다. 이 모델은 평가를 통과할 수 있으며 현재 실제 공격자의 악용은 관찰되지 않았다고 밝히고, 모델 가중치 감사와 에이전트 권한 제한 등을 방어책으로 제시한다.

curation.reason_ko: Microsoft 연구는 뉴런 편집으로 잠복형 모델 백도어를 만들 수 있다고 보고했으며 실제 악용은 관찰되지 않았다고 밝혔다.

2cdb5f24496c894dc15c7641.summary_ko: 연구진은 동형암호 기반 비대화형 트랜스포머 추론 구조 MOAI를 제안했다. 초록에 따르면 회전 연산을 줄여 BERT-base에서 기존 방식보다 동형암호 회전 수가 최소 1.7배 적고, THOR 대비 평가 시간이 52.8% 감소했으며 Powerformer 적용에서도 55.7% 감소했다고 보고했다.
2cdb5f24496c894dc15c7641.background_ko: 클라우드에서 LLM 추론 시 개인정보 우려가 제기됐고, 동형암호는 해결책으로 거론되지만 계산 부담이 큰 점이 연구 배경이다.

curation.reason_ko: 논문은 암호화된 입력으로 트랜스포머 추론을 수행하는 기법의 효율 개선을 보고했다.

806755bd7b4d0b3fcb2ed0ca.title_ko: 미 제재 중국 군 관련 대학, 엔비디아 H200 구매…서버 임대로도 확보
806755bd7b4d0b3fcb2ed0ca.summary_ko: 로이터가 확인한 조달 기록에 따르면 서북공업대는 중국 업체를 통해 H200 2개를 구매했고, H200 8개가 탑재된 서버 임대 계약도 체결했다. 다만 구매 칩의 실제 사용 목적과 유통 경로는 확인되지 않았으며, 서버 계약은 AI 모델 미세조정·강화학습용으로 기재돼 수출통제의 허점 논란이 제기됐다.
806755bd7b4d0b3fcb2ed0ca.background_ko: 서북공업대학은 미사일 확산 및 군사 연구 관여를 이유로 2001년 미국 거래제한기업목록에 올랐고 2019년 제재가 강화됐다.

curation.reason_ko: 미국 제재 대상 중국 대학의 H200 구매 보도로 AI 반도체 수출 통제의 허점이 제기됐다.

hot.reason_ko: 실제 공격 악용이 확인된 Chrome 취약점에 보안 업데이트가 배포돼 이용자 영향이 크다.
인증 우회 취약점이 실제 악용돼 관리자 권한과 연결된 XCP-ng 호스트 root 권한까지 노릴 수 있다.
CISA가 실제 악용 취약점으로 지정했으며 로그인 없이 민감한 설정 파일에 접근할 수 있다.
마이크로소프트가 치명적 결함과 RCE를 포함한 1,235개 취약점을 수정해 영향 범위가 넓다.
국내 금융보안 평가 시스템이 해킹돼 금융회사 제출 자료와 이용자 개인정보가 유출됐다.
SGLang 원격 코드 실행 취약점이 악용돼 서버와 사용자 계정·AI 대화 기록이 유출됐다.
빌드 인프라 침해로 소스 코드와 고객 환경 변수에 접근했고 최대 10만 워크스페이스가 영향권이다.
일본 니토리에서 최대 약 3,762만 건의 개인정보 유출 가능성이 제기돼 규모가 크다.
탈취된 Qubole IAM 자격 증명으로 고객 AWS 환경에 침입해 데이터와 비밀 정보를 탈취했다.
ScreenConnect 공격으로 MSP 6곳과 47개 조직의 엔드포인트 286대 이상이 영향을 받았다.

CVE-2026-126262.description: A improper neutralization of special elements used in an sql command ('sql injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiManager 8.0.0, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.12 may allow an unauthenticated attacker who has access to the oftp port to execute code or command on the system via crafted OFTP packets.
CVE-2026-126262.summary_ko: FortiAnalyzer 및 FortiManager의 SQL 인젝션 취약점으로, OFTP 포트에 접근 가능한 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 OFTP 패킷을 통해 시스템에서 코드나 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiAnalyzer와 FortiManager의 OFTP 처리 결함으로 비인증 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-126259.description: A missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.12, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.13 may allow an unauthenticated attacker with HA FGSP + standalone-config-sync, or autoscale to execute command as super admin via crafted HA packets.
CVE-2026-126259.summary_ko: FortiOS의 중요 기능에 인증이 누락된 취약점입니다. 특정 HA 구성 또는 오토스케일 환경에서 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 HA 패킷으로 슈퍼 관리자 권한의 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 특정 FortiOS 구성에서 인증 없이 슈퍼 관리자 권한 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-126147.description: A improper limitation of a pathname to a restricted directory ('path traversal') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiMail 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiMail 7.6.0 through 7.6.6, FortiMail 7.4.0 through 7.4.8, FortiMail 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted requests.
CVE-2026-126147.summary_ko: FortiMail의 경로 순회 취약점으로, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 요청을 통해 허가되지 않은 코드나 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiMail의 경로 순회로 비인증 공격자가 코드나 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-126148.description: A improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiMail 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiMail 7.6.0 through 7.6.6 may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted HA join-request packets.
CVE-2026-126148.summary_ko: Fortinet FortiMail에서 OS 명령어 삽입 취약점이 발견되었습니다. 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 HA 가입 요청 패킷을 전송하여 무단 코드나 명령어를 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiMail의 HA 가입 요청 처리에서 비인증 OS 명령 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-126164.description: A improper neutralization of special elements used in an sql command ('sql injection') vulnerability in Fortinet FortiMail 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiMail 7.6.0 through 7.6.6, FortiMail 7.4.0 through 7.4.8, FortiMail 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via crafted requests.
CVE-2026-126164.summary_ko: FortiMail의 SQL 인젝션 취약점으로, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 요청을 통해 허가되지 않은 코드나 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiMail의 SQL 인젝션으로 비인증 코드나 명령 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-126170.description: A improper encoding or escaping of output vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 8.0.1 through 8.0.2, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer-BigData 7.6.0 through 7.6.2, FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.2, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.1 through 8.0.2, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7 may allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute unauthorized code or commands via a specially crafted HTTP request
CVE-2026-126170.summary_ko: FortiAnalyzer, FortiAnalyzer Cloud, FortiAnalyzer-BigData, FortiManager 및 FortiManager Cloud의 출력 인코딩 취약점으로, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 조작된 HTTP 요청을 통해 허가되지 않은 코드나 명령을 실행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Fortinet 관리 제품의 HTTP 요청 처리 결함으로 비인증 코드나 명령 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-126150.description: A weak password recovery mechanism for forgotten password vulnerability in Fortinet FortiMail 8.0.0, FortiMail 7.6.0 through 7.6.5, FortiMail 7.4.0 through 7.4.7, FortiMail 7.2.0 through 7.2.9 may allow an unauthenticated attacker to reset the password of an arbitrary IBE webmail user and take over their account via specially crafted HTTP requests.
CVE-2026-126150.summary_ko: Fortinet FortiMail의 취약한 비밀번호 복구 기능으로 비인증 공격자가 임의의 IBE 웹메일 사용자 비밀번호를 재설정하고 계정을 탈취할 수 있다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiMail의 비밀번호 복구 취약점으로 IBE 웹메일 계정을 탈취할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-126155.description: A incorrect authorization vulnerability in Fortinet FortiMail 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiMail 7.6.0 through 7.6.6, FortiMail 7.4.0 through 7.4.8, FortiMail 7.2 all versions may allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain an authenticated IBE webmail session as any IBE recipient and read or send their encrypted mail via crafted HTTP requests.
CVE-2026-126155.summary_ko: Fortinet FortiMail의 잘못된 권한 부여 취약점으로 비인증 원격 공격자가 임의의 IBE 수신자 인증 세션을 얻어 암호화된 메일을 읽거나 보낼 수 있다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiMail에서 비인증 공격자가 IBE 수신자의 메일 세션을 얻을 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-126229.description: A authorization bypass through user-controlled key vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiAnalyzer 7.0 all versions, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 8.0.1, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.12, FortiAnalyzer Cloud 7.0 all versions, FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiManager 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager 7.4.0 through 7.4.11, FortiManager 7.2.0 through 7.2.12, FortiManager 7.0 all versions, FortiManager Cloud 8.0.1, FortiManager Cloud 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiManager Cloud 7.4.1 through 7.4.11, FortiManager Cloud 7.2.1 through 7.2.12, FortiManager Cloud 7.0 all versions may allow an authenticated administrator to access to other VDOMs via specially crafted HTTP requests.

curation.reason_ko: FortiAnalyzer와 FortiManager에서 다른 VDOM에 접근할 수 있는 권한 우회입니다.

CVE-2026-126251.description: A incorrect authorization vulnerability in Fortinet FortiAuthenticator 8.0.0 through 8.0.3, FortiAuthenticator 6.6.0 through 6.6.10 may allow an attacker to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access.
CVE-2026-126251.summary_ko: FortiAuthenticator의 잘못된 권한 부여 취약점으로, 공격자가 인증을 우회해 허가되지 않은 접근 권한을 얻을 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiAuthenticator의 인증 우회로 허가되지 않은 접근이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-126254.description: A numeric truncation error vulnerability in Fortinet FortiOS 8.0.0 through 8.0.1, FortiOS 7.6.0 through 7.6.7, FortiOS 7.4.0 through 7.4.12, FortiOS 7.2.0 through 7.2.13 may allow a configured ibgp neighbor to send malicious/malformed attributes to all connected routers via a specially crafted request
CVE-2026-126254.summary_ko: Fortinet FortiOS의 숫자 절단 오류 취약점으로, 설정된 iBGP 이웃이 악성 또는 잘못된 속성을 연결된 모든 라우터에 보낼 수 있다.

curation.reason_ko: FortiOS의 iBGP 처리 결함으로 연결된 라우터에 악성 속성을 전파할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123710.description: A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. An unauthenticated client can obtain an anonymous registry token with an audience it controls, present that token to the service key rotation endpoint, and install its own approved signing key with no expiry. Registry tokens signed with that key are accepted for any repository, allowing read and write access to private images and replacement of repository tags.
CVE-2026-123710.summary_ko: Red Hat Quay의 레지스트리 토큰 처리 결함입니다. 인증되지 않은 클라이언트가 임의의 서명 키를 등록하여 사설 이미지에 대한 읽기 및 쓰기 권한을 얻고 태그를 교체할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Red Hat Quay의 서명 키 취약점으로 사설 이미지의 읽기·쓰기와 태그 변경이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-110697.description: A flaw was found in Quay where the robot account listing function constructs a SQL LIKE pattern from user-controlled namespace names without escaping wildcard metacharacters. An attacker who creates a namespace containing an underscore character can match and retrieve robot accounts and their decrypted authentication tokens from other tenants' namespaces, leading to cross-tenant credential theft and unauthorized image operations.
CVE-2026-110697.summary_ko: Quay의 로봇 계정 목록 기능에서 SQL LIKE 패턴 생성 시 와일드카드를 적절히 처리하지 않아 발생하는 취약점입니다. 공격자가 특정 네임스페이스를 생성하여 타 테넌트의 로봇 계정 정보와 복호화된 인증 토큰을 탈취하고 무단 이미지 작업을 수행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Quay의 취약점으로 다른 테넌트의 로봇 계정 토큰을 탈취할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-119618.description: Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization vulnerability in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 in assign_headers() can lead to RCE. This issue affects Apache HTTP Server: from 2.4.55 through 2.4.70. Affected releases of mod_h2 from GitHub: from 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
CVE-2026-119618.summary_ko: Apache HTTP Server의 mod_http2에서 공유 자원 동기화 오류로 발생하는 원격 코드 실행 취약점입니다. 헤더 할당 과정에서의 결함이 영향을 미칩니다.

curation.reason_ko: Apache HTTP Server mod_http2의 동기화 결함이 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-126325.description: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability has been reported in PTC Windchill and PTC FlexPLM. The vulnerability may be exploited through the deserialization of untrusted data.
CVE-2026-126325.summary_ko: PTC Windchill 및 FlexPLM에서 발생하는 치명적인 원격 코드 실행 취약점입니다. 신뢰할 수 없는 데이터의 역직렬화 과정을 통해 악용될 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: PTC Windchill 및 FlexPLM에서 신뢰할 수 없는 데이터 역직렬화로 원격 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-123864.description: A re-entrancy flaw in Node.js HTTPS lets an unauthenticated client read memory belonging to other connections, including TLS private keys and other users' requests. TLSWrap::DoWrite() calls ClearOut() directly when asked to write zero bytes; if that write is issued from JavaScript running inside the HTTP parser's on_body callback, ClearOut() decrypts the next TLS record while the parser is still mid-body, re-entering llhttp_execute() and causing a use-after-free and an out-of-bounds heap read. The server then copies that freed or unrelated heap memory into the response for the request body. Triggering it requires a handler that calls res.flushHeaders() before the request body ends and later calls res.end() with a non-empty chunk, and reading the leaked memory requires any ordinary route that echoes or stores a request body. Cleartext node:http is not affected. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
CVE-2026-123864.summary_ko: Node.js HTTPS 모듈의 재진입 결함으로 인한 메모리 유출 취약점입니다. TLS 비공개 키를 포함한 타인의 요청 데이터를 공격자가 읽을 수 있으며, 힙 메모리 손상이 발생합니다.

curation.reason_ko: Node.js HTTPS의 재진입 결함으로 TLS 비공개 키 등 연결 간 메모리가 노출될 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123872.description: A client certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS lets a client change the servername during TLS 1.2 renegotiation to reach endpoints it was not authorized for. On a server that applies different client-certificate policies per hostname, for example stricter admin-only client-cert auth on one host and ordinary client-cert auth on another, a client that authenticates for a permitted host can renegotiate the TLS 1.2 connection under a different servername and carry its existing authentication to the protected host, bypassing the stricter policy. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
CVE-2026-123872.summary_ko: Node.js 26.x, 24.x, 22.x의 TLS에서 클라이언트 인증서 인증 우회가 발생할 수 있다. TLS 1.2 재협상 중 서버 이름을 바꾸면 허용된 호스트의 기존 인증이 더 엄격한 정책의 보호 호스트에 적용될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-123872.background_ko: TLS 1.2 재협상 중 서버 이름을 변경해 기존 클라이언트 인증을 다른 호스트에 적용할 수 있는 것이 원인이다.

curation.reason_ko: Node.js TLS의 인증 우회로 호스트별 클라이언트 인증 정책을 건너뛸 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123866.description: A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connections' response buffers, to a peer. When a stream is torn down while a write is still backpressured, for example by a peer RST_STREAM or by the server's own per-stream timeout destroying the stream, the stream's response buffer is freed but a reference to it is still used, so freed or unrelated heap memory is written to the socket instead of the intended response. On Node.js 26.x and 24.x the teardown can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present, and on all supported lines the same defect is reachable through an application-initiated teardown such as a per-stream idle timeout. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.
CVE-2026-123866.summary_ko: Node.js HTTP/2 스트림 종료 과정의 해제 후 사용 취약점으로, 의도한 응답 대신 다른 연결의 응답 버퍼를 포함한 메모리 내용이 상대방에게 노출될 수 있습니다. Node.js 26.x, 24.x, 22.x가 영향을 받습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Node.js HTTP/2의 해제 후 사용 결함으로 다른 연결의 응답 메모리가 노출될 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-123863.description: A reachable assertion in Node.js HTTP/2 session teardown lets any unauthenticated client abort the server, over both TLS and cleartext. A client can arrange for an Http2Stream that still holds nghttp2-allocated header buffers to outlive its session: the stream is removed from the session's stream set but never detached, so when ~Http2Session() runs the memory accounting is nonzero and the CHECK_EQ(current_nghttp2_memory_, 0) assertion fails, terminating the process. The trigger needs only a default http2 server whose handler responds before the request body has ended, which is typical. It is a variant of CVE-2024-27983 that the earlier fix did not cover, because that fix only detached streams still tracked in the session. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x (since 26.9.0) and 24.x (since 24.22.0).
CVE-2026-123863.summary_ko: Node.js HTTP/2 세션 종료 과정의 검증 취약점으로, 인증되지 않은 클라이언트가 서버 프로세스를 종료시킬 수 있습니다. Node.js 26.x와 24.x가 영향을 받습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Node.js HTTP/2의 세션 종료 결함으로 비인증 원격 사용자가 서버를 중단시킬 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-67544.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.71, Heym's workflow engine accepts an arbitrary Python code string in the playwrightCode field of a Playwright node. This string is written to a temporary .py file and executed directly by the backend process via subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, script_path]) with no sandboxing, AST validation, or role gate. Any authenticated user — including a freshly registered account — can achieve full remote code execution (RCE) on the backend host, running as the service process user (observed as root in the default Docker deployment). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.71.
CVE-2026-67544.summary_ko: Heym 워크플로우 엔진에서 파이썬 코드를 검증 없이 실행하는 취약점입니다. 인증된 사용자는 샌드박스나 역할 제한 없이 백엔드 호스트에서 원격 코드 실행(RCE)을 수행할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Heym 워크플로우에서 검증되지 않은 Python 코드를 실행해 백엔드 원격 코드 실행이 가능합니다.

CVE-2026-67543.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, heym hardens one untrusted-code path but not its sibling. The Python tool executor (python_tool_executor.py) treats user code as untrusted and mandates a Docker sandbox (no network, read-only fs, non-root, no docker socket), failing closed. The skill executor (skill_python_executor.py) runs skill Python via a local backend subprocess with no Docker isolation — only a 512 MB RLIMIT and a 7-key env denylist — so a skill executes inside the backend execution context, with filesystem access, network egress, and non-denylisted environment variables that should not be exposed to untrusted/shared skills. In the shipped Docker config (backend runs as root + /var/run/docker.sock mounted), this escalates to host root. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.
CVE-2026-67543.summary_ko: Heym 0.0.70 이전 버전은 스킬의 Python 코드를 격리 없이 실행해 파일 시스템·네트워크 등에 접근하게 할 수 있다. 제공된 Docker 설정에서는 호스트 root 권한까지 확대될 수 있다.
CVE-2026-67543.background_ko: 스킬 실행기가 Python 코드를 Docker 격리 없이 로컬 백엔드 하위 프로세스로 실행하는 것이 원인이다.

curation.reason_ko: Heym의 skill 실행기가 격리되지 않아 백엔드 파일과 환경에 접근할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-67546.description: Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.75, the same POST /api/mcp/fetch-tools endpoint (any authenticated user, lowest role) also accepts the stdio transport, which spawns the attacker-supplied command with attacker-supplied args and an environment merged over os.environ. The process executes on the shared backend host before MCP protocol validation fails — so side effects fire regardless of whether the command speaks MCP. This is a distinct weakness class and exploit primitive from the SSRF (Advisory 2) on the same endpoint, and needs a different fix (role gating / opt-in trust boundary rather than egress controls). This issue has been patched in version 0.0.75.
CVE-2026-67546.summary_ko: Heym 0.0.75 이전 버전의 취약점으로 인증된 사용자가 공유 백엔드 호스트에서 임의 명령을 실행해 부작용을 일으킬 수 있다.
CVE-2026-67546.background_ko: 해당 엔드포인트가 stdio 전송을 허용해 프로토콜 검증 전에 명령을 실행하는 것이 원인이다.

curation.reason_ko: Heym의 MCP 도구 요청이 공격자 제공 명령을 백엔드 호스트에서 실행할 수 있습니다.

CVE-2026-76954.description: An improper neutralization of special elements used in an SQL command vulnerability in the Auth API in Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 7.2.1-69057-13, 7.2.2-72806-10, 7.3.2-86009-5, and 7.4.1-90080-1 allows remote attackers to read or write arbitrary files and conduct denial-of-service attacks.

CVE-2026-13672.summary_ko: Synology DiskStation Manager의 SSOAuth 권한 우회 취약점으로, 인증된 원격 사용자가 임의 파일을 읽거나 쓰고 서비스 거부 공격을 할 수 있다.

CVE-2026-18792.summary_ko: Synology DSM의 Sharing API에서 제한 디렉터리 경로 제한이 부적절한 취약점으로, 원격 인증 사용자가 임의 파일을 읽거나 쓰고 서비스 거부를 일으킬 수 있다.

curation.reason_ko: 악의적인 저장소를 재귀적으로 클론할 때 코드 실행이 가능한 Git 취약점이 패치됐다.

curation.reason_ko: SGLang 취약점 악용으로 NEAR AI의 에이전트와 사용자 데이터가 탈취되는 피해가 발생했습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Xen Orchestra 인증 우회 취약점(VSA-2026-062) 패치 및 긴급 업데이트가 권고됩니다.

ede7971fdf6908f2dbf1eef4.summary_ko: AhsayCBS 백업 솔루션의 취약점(CVE-2026-105133, 105134)을 악용한 공격이 발견되어 주의가 필요합니다. 공격자는 웹쉘과 암호화폐 채굴기를 설치하고, 호스트 기기 정보를 식별하여 샌드박스 환경에서 실행을 방지하는 파이썬 기반 백도어를 사용했습니다. 백업 인프라 내 자격 증명을 탈취하려는 시도가 확인되었으며, 해당 취약점은 2026년 10월 중순 패치되었습니다.

17f0720597dfe02caded396f.title_ko: 랜섬웨어 복구 과정의 투명성과 MSP의 고객 유지 전략
17f0720597dfe02caded396f.summary_ko: 랜섬웨어 공격 이후 기술적인 복구가 성공해도, 복구 과정의 불투명한 의사소통이나 예상치 못한 비용 발생은 MSP(관리형 서비스 제공업체)와 고객 간의 신뢰를 무너뜨릴 수 있습니다. Kaseya는 복구 시간 단축과 신뢰 유지를 위해 모니터링, 티켓팅, 백업을 통합한 플랫폼 활용과 명확한 복구 타임라인 제시의 중요성을 강조합니다.

53672ed9f35f2e0e248c42a4.title_original: Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft
53672ed9f35f2e0e248c42a4.excerpt: CVE-2026-124194 is the Outlook zero-day for which Microsoft says it’s aware of active exploitation. The post Exploited Outlook Zero-Day Among 1,094 Flaws Patched by Microsoft appeared first on SecurityWeek .
53672ed9f35f2e0e248c42a4.title_ko: 마이크로소프트 11월 보안 업데이트, Outlook 제로데이 취약점 패치
53672ed9f35f2e0e248c42a4.summary_ko: 마이크로소프트가 11월 패치 화요일을 맞아 Outlook에서 실제 공격에 활용된 제로데이 취약점(CVE-2026-124194)을 포함한 1,094개의 보안 결함을 해결했다. 해당 취약점은 스푸핑 유형으로, 사용자가 공격자의 파일을 열면 NTLMv2 해시가 노출될 위험이 있어 최신 보안 업데이트 설치가 필요하다.

curation.reason_ko: Microsoft가 실제 악용된 Outlook 제로데이를 포함한 대규모 보안 업데이트를 배포했다.

c50f6b846a3fccdc0ee56eec.excerpt: Adobe has fixed vulnerabilities in AEM, Premiere, Photoshop, After Effects, Connect, Audition, Dimension, Content Credentials SDK, and Media Encoder. The post Adobe Patches 110 Vulnerabilities Across 9 Products appeared first on SecurityWeek .
c50f6b846a3fccdc0ee56eec.title_ko: 어도비, 9개 제품군 내 110개 취약점 해결 보안 업데이트 발표
c50f6b846a3fccdc0ee56eec.summary_ko: 어도비(Adobe)가 11월 패치 화요일을 맞아 9개 제품군에 존재하는 약 110개의 취약점을 수정했습니다. Adobe Connect와 AEM 등에서 CVSS 10점의 치명적 취약점이 보고되었으며, 이들은 권한 상승이나 임의 코드 실행에 악용될 수 있습니다. 어도비는 현재 해당 취약점들이 실제 공격에 악용된 사례는 없다고 밝혔습니다.

7688af39dd52e86c4e2793db.title_original: Software Transparency Is Changing: Allan Friedman on SBOM, AI BOMs and What Comes Next
7688af39dd52e86c4e2793db.excerpt: SBOM pioneer Allan Friedman joined the SecurityWeek Podcast to discuss why knowing what is inside software is only the beginning, how AI is complicating software supply chain visibility, and what organizations should be doing with SBOM data once they have it. The post Software Transparency Is Changing: Allan Friedman on SBOM, AI BOMs and What Comes Next appeared first on SecurityWeek .

7688af39dd52e86c4e2793db.summary_ko: 사이버 보안 전문가 앨런 프리드먼은 소프트웨어 공급망 보안을 위해 구성 요소의 가시성을 확보하는 SBOM(Software Bill of Materials)의 중요성을 강조했습니다. 또한 AI 모델과 데이터 출처를 추적하는 AI BOM의 필요성이 커지고 있으며, 취약점의 실제 악용 가능성을 식별하는 VEX(Vulnerability Exploitability eXchange)를 결합하여 대응 효율을 높여야 한다고 설명했습니다.

4710db9f53a1d6134fe7a8da.excerpt: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month’s Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws — including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook — and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe , Apple , Google and Mozilla . Image: Shutterstock.com. Diorama by @zepp1969. November’s patch release from Redmond tackles 1,093 vulnerabilities, fixing 63 “critical” flaws that can be exploited to seize control over a Windows system with little or no help from users. Nearly half of those critical bugs are remote code execution vulnerabilities. Overall, 535 of the flaws addressed this month allow an attacker to elevate their privileges on a vulnerable device. This latest round of updates means Microsoft has shipped more than 5,100 security patches so far this year, a staggering number considering that a year ago Microsoft was averaging around 100 patches per month. Microsoft credits advances in artificial intelligence for helping to find (and fix) such a large volume of security bugs in recent months. Last month, Microsoft pushed more than 1,400 fixes. According to Redmond, just one of the flaws is already seeing active exploitation: CVE-2026-124194 , a spoofing bug in Outlook. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Complete human-agent and agent-agent transcripts enable an audit that reconstructs decision provenance and characterizes the division of cognitive labor. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. Provenance showed that 59-68% of error corrections involved multiple participants and that about half of all decisions incorporated the input of another participant. These results may guide design principles for multi-agent scientific systems and inform future agent harnesses, model training, and accessible autonomous experimentation.

9affa9cd6dc2b2dba93c2c3d.title_original: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
9affa9cd6dc2b2dba93c2c3d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. Two controls test what answers rest on: the closed book removes the record, and instrument pairs alter one satellite's data while nothing changes on the ground. Evaluations of twelve multimodal agents reveal that leading agents complete most analyses end to end but falter when an answer requires mapping from imagery. Further analysis shows that the record moves answers from prior knowledge to the pixels but not yet to the real change on the ground: when one satellite's data are altered, half of the right answers follow the alteration. EarthRecord thus provides a principled platform for measuring and advancing agents from pixels to land change.

05a4d97cbf13375a4f2dc273.title_original: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
05a4d97cbf13375a4f2dc273.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. Ablations conducted to understand the contribution of the SAE revealed that classifiers reaching baseline performance without it were several times larger. Our findings show that compact topic monitors can be trained inexpensively in prefill and deployed during generation. More broadly, our work shows where SAEs are useful beyond safety classification. Our code, dataset and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mercity-AI/SAE-Guardrails and https://huggingface.co/collections/Mercity/online-guardrails-using-sparse-autoencoders-6ac602940468c62fefb2b9e8

a03923671dff1cfe378fc56d.title_original: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
a03923671dff1cfe378fc56d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. To support training and evaluation in this domain, we also present LandslideVL, the first benchmark for intelligent landslide analysis, combining visual imagery and newly introduced textual prompts. Comprehensive experiments across public datasets and LandslideVL demonstrate that LandslideFM achieves superior quantitative and qualitative performance. Most importantly, LandslideFM surpasses general-purpose VLMs in specialized landslide reasoning and scene analysis. Our code is released at https://github.com/wangshanwen001/LandslideFM.

604d123d8dbb01e5a37c0cfa.title_original: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
604d123d8dbb01e5a37c0cfa.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. Contrastive direction analysis finds geometry aligned with the human matrix in larger instruct variants, but little alignment in base variants under this assay. Across models, geometry strength is associated with behavioral amplification (r = 0.68, p = 0.008; partial r = 0.69 controlling for log size). To relate internal structure to output behavior, a matched activation-probing paradigm shows that probe slopes vary less than behavioral slopes (1.38-1.77 vs 0.52-1.53). A synthetic control shows that ridge probing can inflate these slopes; after subtracting a baseline based on a reliability proxy from another analysis, adjusted slopes remain associated with behavior (r = 0.88). We term the measured probe-behavior gap readout attenuat

e2b5a53e422d5f716f67493a.title_original: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
e2b5a53e422d5f716f67493a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. Taken together, the results indicate that visual prompting primarily aids KGQA by enhancing prediction precision in low-complexity contexts, provided that visual design respects cognitive and perceptual constraints. To optimize both accuracy and inference efficiency, we argue for adaptive visual prompting policies that selectively append diagrams to small, visually sparse subgraphs with well-structured layouts, avoiding unnecessary visual clutter and token overhead on complex queries. We conclude by relating these findi

a628563961f16f3e8af252d3.title_original: Reinforcement Learning based control of Cancer Chemotherapy treatments
a628563961f16f3e8af252d3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement Learning has achieved tremendous success in recent years. Extending its scope from the traditional complex games such as Atari, Go, Pokeman, and Chess, reinforcement learning has caught researchers' attention on modelling real-life scenarios. Personalized medicine and the dynamic treatment regimen are two such preliminary research fields; researchers are focusing their mindsets currently. Estimating the optimal dynamic treatment regimens from the observational real clinical data is being popularized among the researchers, widening its scope towards more advanced versions of reinforcement learning algorithms. This research is about a research study that focused on reinforcement learning techniques that have been approached in the context of cancer chemotherapy treatments. Primarily this thesis addresses the result of the study by means of the state-of-the-art on reinforcement learning techniques used in generating the optimal policy for sequential treatments, including the existing online reinforcement learning approaches. Thereby a simulation for cancer chemotherapy via traditional Q-learning would be presented. Secondly, the study will extend towards using offline reinforcement learning in the optimal policy generation. Thus, the proposed solution follows a data-driven approach, which works on the real human colon cancer clinical data. The novelty of the proposed solution resides in the implementation of an offlin

8f76b02d8047e768a61e170d.title_original: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
8f76b02d8047e768a61e170d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. An analytic bound supported by the simulations shows that intelligence-driven speedup is capped by the ratio of competing intelligence levels regardless of task difficulty. The simulations also expose a fast-takeoff dilemma: a large intelligence-driven speedup multiplier materializes only when the hypothesis space is noisy, but the absolute timescale remains constrained by the time required for capability-critical tests, so a large multiplier need not imply rapid progress. Simulations also indicate that institutional chokepoints disproportionately slow down superintelligent agents when mandatory authorization delays are large

413c1a371e57b80b36589e6a.title_original: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
413c1a371e57b80b36589e6a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. On Orange it is ahead in all 10 splits (14.3%), but the gain is not significant after correction (Holm p = 0.155). The splits resample the same datasets, so these results do not stand for independent operators. TabICL v2, the earlier benchmark's leader, beats the best tuned GBDT only on Iranian, not all three of them, and underpredicts Orange churn by 2.1 points on a 7.3% base rate. On the datasets and splits where we tested them, a substantially larger tuning budget and a duplicate-aware split leave the ma

4639ed8212f7e73d71977928.title_original: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
4639ed8212f7e73d71977928.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change relative to the mean change of its own set, and then compares changes from the two models that were induced by the same perturbation. On LeaFBench, SetPrint consistently outperforms existing training-free black-box fingerprinting methods. Further analyses attribute these gains to both within-set relations and between-set correspondence.

cc953d6e93989cd5931edbab.title_original: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
cc953d6e93989cd5931edbab.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to build matched high and low-quality skill corpora. Three takeaways emerge. (1)~\textbf{There is no universal best architecture; the right choice is SOP-dependent.} On a given SOP, task success ranges from under $10\%$ on the hardest to near $100\%$ on the easiest; no architecture is statistically separable in aggregate, and added structure only plausibly pays off on complex, branching SOPs (a directional, not yet significant, trend). (2)~\textbf{Added architecture cost must be justified by a task-success gain.} Every coordinated arm (multi-agent or skill-augmented) spends $1.4$--$4.7\times$ the tokens and $2.6$--$5.8\times$ the latency of the single agent for gains that are usually small and rarely significant, making the single agent the efficient default; high-quality skills do lift success (to $73.1\%$ from $67.4\%$) while degraded skills fall below it. 26a4b2c247a9c361043936e7.title_original: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
26a4b2c247a9c361043936e7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. Experiments on four PDEs, namely the heat, advection, Burgers', and Allen--Cahn equations, demonstrate lower solution errors than conventional physics-informed neural networks, while revealing limitations in satisfying the governing equations for nonlinear PDEs.

1b31032fffd2d5bf1bb9f4ce.title_original: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
1b31032fffd2d5bf1bb9f4ce.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiment

9008f771260c6d95e01a369c.title_original: Monitoring One Channel Is Not Communication Control: Causal Evidence for Adaptive Reallocation of Joint Message--Route Codes
9008f771260c6d95e01a369c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. In two independent 20-seed batches, 20/20 and 19/20 protocols form. Online partial coverage increases shadow-route share over no monitoring by .701 [.574,.826] and .575 [.412,.737], while task accuracy remains .905/.913 and signed frozen message contribution remains .592/.563. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. A corrected explicit-silence cost makes 18/20 policies fully silent and lowers mean sending to .050, but its strict complete-suppression gate fails because two seeds retain communication. Failed semantic-evasion and operational gates further bound the result. The evidence supports adaptive reallocation of a joint message--route code under partial monitoring, not open-world route discovery, emergent encryption, or a universal defense.

88dc3028225c57bea2312b6b.title_original: IIT Patna at "ICPR 2026 TVRID Competition on Privacy-Preserving Person Re-Identification from Top-View RGB-Depth Camera"
88dc3028225c57bea2312b6b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Privacy-aware person re-identification (Re-ID) from top-view cameras replaces frontal appearance with anthropometric shape, while depth sensing further reduces color-based identity cues. The ICPR 2026 TVRID competition evaluates this setting using 86 identities captured by four synchronized Intel RealSense D455 cameras with RGB and Depth streams across flat, ascent, descent, and oblique viewpoints. Performance is measured using mAP and CMC@1 across within-camera in/out, ascent-descent, and flat-oblique scenarios. The competition had 147 registered participants and 33 final submissions. Three teams from IIT Patna participated: 'abhinavkumar03' and 'sjkdgfhl_' ranked 5th and 7th among 31 ranked participants, and 'vivek katuri' reached 77.67% CMC@1 / 85.20% mAP on the RGB track. This paper presents the methods of the two top-10 teams. Methodology 1 (abhinavkumar03) achieves 93.51% mAP and 90.42% CMC@1 on Depth, ranking 4th of 28, while Methodology 2 (sjkdgfhl_) reaches 99.63%/99.35% on RGB and 86.26%/80.34% on Depth. Both substantially outperform the 57.19% track-average Depth mAP, with Methodology 1 yielding a 7.3-point gain over Methodology 2. These results demonstrate the importance of depth representation and supervision for privacy-preserving Re-ID.

d5ca9308efeac3800bab1cd8.title_original: RBLA+: Efficient Rank-Specific LoRA Adapter Extraction for Federated Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Clients
d5ca9308efeac3800bab1cd8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12961v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces communication and computational overhead by training and exchanging compact trainable LoRA factors. Clients may use different LoRA ranks to meet adapter communication budgets and accommodate different local adaptation needs. The server must process these differences during aggregation and construct adapters at each client's rank for local training. We distinguish pre-aggregation alignment, which handles factor dimensions and scaling conventions before aggregation and rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction, which constructs client-sized pairs from the aggregated global model. Two common approaches to rank-specific extraction are direct rank truncation and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the dense update. Direct prefix truncation keeps the leading columns of one aggregated factor and the corresponding rows of the other. It is cheap but can increase reconstruction error. The dense SVD approach first forms the product of aggregated LoRA factors. It then decomposes this matrix and retains the leading singular components to construct adapters at the target rank. This gives the optimal rank-constrained approximation in Frobenius norm but incurs significant computational overhead. To address this trade-off, we propose RBLA+ as an extension of RBLA. b32b326634a62b408bc6506e.title_original: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
b32b326634a62b408bc6506e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We introduce \textsc{BuySideFlow}, a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks spanning equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics over a fixed snapshot from a licensed production financial database. We provide executable references and a taxonomy of temporal errors, pairing result checks with expert audits of executed workflows. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging from 16.2\% to 36.8\%. An audit of 900 runs on 100 shared tasks confirms PIT violations in 193 of the 380 runs that pass result checks (50.8\%), showing that output agreement alone does not establish temporal validity.

78355b77e3a9d0013ace0669.title_original: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation
78355b77e3a9d0013ace0669.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. We introduce TrustMod-SM, a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets, to evaluate LLM moderators on five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escalate ambiguous cases, and struggle to separate hate speech from counter-speech or reclaimed language (especially below 8B parameters). Scaling does not uniformly resolve these issues, and no single model excels across all five dimensions.

4dc59980242d879b65513aa6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. We propose ZeroPoint, an EBM that makes the empty answer a state of the model with energy zero for every input. This fixed state provides an explicit reference for the energies of all listed options, whose non-negative depths measure their compatibility with the input relative to the empty answer. The options and the empty answer share one distribution, in which an option at zero depth receives no probability. The decision to select an option or to abstain is thus part of ordinary inference, trained with the negative log-likelihood loss, rather than a separate rejection rule. 3a1897c95090a085e0caa5dd.title_original: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
3a1897c95090a085e0caa5dd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism. On 507 internal cases across five imaging types, MedScope-4B reached ESG 0.758 and claimed an erased lesion in 9.6% of cases, against 0.27-0.47 and 41-62% for the frontier models (all p<0.001), without significant loss of accuracy on real lesions. Without counterfactual views ESG fell to 0.279+-0.107 (three seeds); the effect replicated on MedGemma 1.5 4B and two unseen inpainting tools. At four external centres the advantage held but frontier models detected more real lesions; on a fresh external test MedScope-4B detected 0 of 48 pneumothorax films, with net utility below gemini-4-argon's (-0.36 [-0.50, -0.23]). e5fe98d6fd1232f9897f5891.title_original: From Questions to Decisions: Benchmarking How LLM Agents Acquire Decision-Relevant Information from Human Beings
e5fe98d6fd1232f9897f5891.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents are increasingly asked to make plans for people, such as scheduling drivers or assigning nurses. However, people's requests are often incomplete, and the supporting information for decision-making may be outdated, requiring agents to ask for clarification. Existing benchmarks typically provide fully specified problems or rely on uncalibrated LLM-simulated users, leaving this ability insufficiently tested. We introduce Ask2Decide, a benchmark of 43 planning tasks that evaluates whether agents ask for missing information that matters for their decisions. An operator holds facts absent from the agent's request and records, and optimization solvers determine which facts change the optimal plan. We also include similarly worded facts that leave the optimal plan unchanged to test whether agents distinguish useful information from irrelevant details. We collect 79 interaction sessions from 19 participants and find that, after an incorrect plan, human replies omit the correcting fact far more often than replies from an uncalibrated simulated user (43% versus 7%). Using these interactions, we calibrate a simulated operator that more closely matches human reply patterns. Evaluating four frontier LLMs, we find that their initial plans are infeasible on 58-98% of tasks when information is missing, compared with 5-28% when all facts are provided upfront. Agents uncover facts that change the optimal plan only slightly more often th

203f11e7e8dde87155390ad0.title_original: Multi-Future Drafting: Mixture Block Drafters for Tree-Verified Speculative Decoding
203f11e7e8dde87155390ad0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13017v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block drafters such as DFlash draft a block of future tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees such as DDTree verify the prefixes ranked highest by the product of the drafter's per-position distributions. Under tree verification, the expected number of accepted tokens is the probability mass the tree covers. We show that a product misallocates it: when the continuation can follow several futures, it splices them into chimeras, prefixes stitched together from different futures that the target never produces, and gives them as much budget as the futures themselves. Barring ties, no product-ranked tree can hold two futures that disagree in $m$ positions without $2^{m-1}-1$ chimeras, however well the drafter is trained, and in practice chimeras make up 27-33% of a 64-node tree. We propose Multi-Future Drafting (MFD), which restores the coupling with a latent variable instead of the chain rule: $K$ learned mode embeddings at the drafter's input draft $K$ coherent blocks in the same pass, and a mixture DDTree lets the verifier pick the future the target takes, losslessly and with $K+1$ extra vectors. On four Qwen targets from 4B to 27B parameters, at batch size 1, MFD reaches up to 7.8$\times$ speedup, 5-8% faster than the best single-mode tree trained identically and, on Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, 9-16% faster than the released DARTree trained on the same prompts.

6d6d6defdf63bc2d950ff704.title_original: ChipOmni: A General-Purpose AI Agent for Electronic Design Automation
6d6d6defdf63bc2d950ff704.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13020v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electronic design automation (EDA) workflows remain highly fragmented, requiring engineers to coordinate heterogeneous representations, specialised software tools, and iterative verification across multiple design stages. Although large language models have brought more general reasoning and code-generation capabilities to EDA, many existing approaches remain focused on isolated tasks and struggle to plan, verify, and repair designs autonomously within executable engineering environments. Here we introduce ChipOmni, a knowledge-enhanced, context-evolving AI agent framework for EDA. ChipOmni integrates multimodal understanding, dynamic planning, multi-agent collaboration, and verification-driven tool interaction into a unified autonomous system. By continually incorporating feedback from external engineering tools, the framework maintains an evolving task context, integrates domain knowledge, and iteratively refines intermediate designs. Across benchmarks for analog circuit, RTL, testbench, and formal-assertion generation, ChipOmni improves multiple task-specific measures over the evaluated baselines and solves all 30 AnalogCoder-Pro tasks. In a long-horizon case study, ChipOmni advances a natural-language RISC-V specification through three design levels to a micro-SoC GDSII layout that passes physical sign-off, without human intervention after initialization. Together, these results show that ChipOmni can coordinate verification

d500515f989c5c383e74e74d.title_original: Understanding-First AI Engineering: Purposes, Reference Architecture, and Architectural Patterns for Human Understanding
d500515f989c5c383e74e74d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems can produce reliable results without developing human understanding. However, human understanding remains valuable for shaping subsequent AI-supported work, forming preferences, governing collective choices and satisfying curiosity, even when human participation is unnecessary for correcting errors. We propose understanding-first AI engineering, which treats purpose-specific human understanding as a first-class design principle guiding requirements, design and operation. The purposes of understanding are organised into four complementary rationales: reflective agency, effective action, collective governance and epistemic value. A reference architecture connects production, verification, use, and learning and exploration through shared records, supporting understanding through explanation and participation. Five candidate architectural patterns guide choices about parallel learning, explanatory models, goal exploration, audience-specific views and distributed expertise. Qualitative scenario analysis of two hypothetical use cases demonstrates how the purpose classification, reference architecture and selected patterns guide investigation, participation and decision processes while retaining operational controls. The cases illustrate design consequences and limitations rather than establish empirical effectiveness. The approach makes human understanding an explicit engineering commitment whose justification need not depe

8c5bf10e1e6754b2018cf94f.title_original: GRAP: Gender Rubric-Aware Probing for Analyzing Gender Bias in LLMs
8c5bf10e1e6754b2018cf94f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13024v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs increasingly mediate everyday interactions, subtle gender biases in open-ended responses pose growing societal risks. Existing probing methods have two key limitations: they rely on fixed-format tasks, such as pronoun resolution or occupation association, that alignment-tuned models can easily handle; and they compare raw group-level rubric scores, ignoring per-dimension variance and obscuring which bias dimensions reliably distinguish gender groups. We introduce GRAP (Gender Rubric-Aware Probing), a framework that uses a lightweight logistic probe to identify the most discriminative bias dimensions from responses scored across 10 rubric dimensions, operating task-agnostically on open-ended instruction following.

598d84682e25018d2d955b11.title_original: APS-VLA: Action-Guided and Future-Aware Token Pruning for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Models
598d84682e25018d2d955b11.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies have demonstrated strong generalization in robotic manipulation, yet processing dense visual tokens often incurs high inference latency. Visual token pruning offers a practical way to reduce this cost, but identifying a compact set of tokens that preserves reliable action generation remains challenging. Existing methods largely rely on static or immediate heuristic cues to estimate token importance. We introduce APS-VLA, a framework that learns visual token selection from robot demonstrations while keeping the pretrained VLA backbone frozen. A lightweight Decision Influence Estimator scores tokens conditioned on current visual observations, language instructions, and robot proprioception. Its training combines two complementary signals: action supervision matches both the full-input policy predictions and demonstrated actions, while an auxiliary visual transition objective uses demonstrated actions to predict subsequent visual features from the selected representation. At deployment, the estimator performs a single hard selection and packing step before the policy's native action-generation procedure; the auxiliary predictor is removed. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on LIBERO and with $\pi_{0.5}$ and XR-1 on RoboCasa365 demonstrate inference acceleration with modest changes in task success. Across five real-world tasks on two dual-arm platforms, APS-VLA reduces mean policy inference latency f

11aa1e4c580400bba4fa5087.title_original: Trust, but verify, audit and attribute: a human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced research results
11aa1e4c580400bba4fa5087.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems now produce research results in bulk: in October 2026 a single laboratory released more than 700 AI-generated mathematics manuscripts, only part of them with machine-checked proofs. Such volumes will be checked mostly by AI agents that call specialised software. A passing check certifies only the artefact that was checked. For proofs translated into the proof assistant Lean, it has been shown that this artefact may state something other than the author's text, and that deciding whether a translation is faithful is undecidable in general. The human researcher therefore stays in the loop, and human and AI contributions must be recorded. We propose a domain-independent, human-in-the-loop framework for checking AI-produced results. Validated, agent-usable tools with different grounds of trust check the results; a fidelity audit asks whether each check addressed the claim as stated; the human decides at fixed points; and a dialog report attributes the work to the human and to the AI. We describe two automatic implementations of the tool layer, for mathematics (Wolfram Language, MATLAB, Lean) and statistics (Python and R), and run the mathematical one on a two-claim example. An ambiguous claim was split into two readings, one refuted and one proved.

37ad1ee880971dae4129b1bb.title_original: Elicitation of the parameters of a multi-criteria sorting model
37ad1ee880971dae4129b1bb.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13062v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiple-criteria decision aiding (MCDA) proposes models and methods for different types of decision problems such as choice, ranking or sorting. Such models involve various parameters that must be elicited. In the elicitation process, all necessary information has to be taken from the decision-maker. For this, several direct and indirect elicitation methods are suggested in the literature. In this work, we concentrate on direct elicitation: we aim at providing a rigorous elicitation procedure for the parameters of the Non-Compensatory Sorting model (NCS), which has been characterized by an axiomatic analysis. A basic version of the NCS model is considered, i.e., a model with two categories and no vetoes. The parameters are the set of sufficient coalitions of criteria and the profile separating the two categories. Regarding the sufficient coalitions, we propose several questioning algorithms that engraft questions on classical graph exploration algorithms such as depth-first search. Such algorithms are implemented and evaluated by simulation. For eliciting the limit profile, we design a questioning algorithm using dichotomy. Questioning algorithms can be optimal in the worst case or on average. An optimal algorithm in the worst case has been proposed by Hansel in the framework of monotone Boolean functions. We implement and evaluate this algorithm as a variant of the depth-first search approaches. Regarding optimal questioning s

0a814180120de711fef0d4ec.title_original: Building World Models from Intrinsic Motivation
0a814180120de711fef0d4ec.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the absence of extrinsic rewards or task supervision, human behavior is guided by intrinsic motivation---neural signals that drive curiosity, creativity, play, and other essential facets of intelligence. Intrinsic motivation plays an important developmental role in building robust world models that enable generalization and adaptation. Yet existing studies leave open how a broad range of intrinsic motivations interacts with world-model representation learning to support downstream control. This limits our understanding of which intrinsically collected experiences build reusable models. To address these gaps, we integrate 24 intrinsic objectives, including established methods and explicit variants spanning curiosity, entropy, and competency, into a common model-based reinforcement learning framework. We evaluate the world models they build through zero-shot, few-shot, and multi-task control in locomotion, manipulation, and open-ended gaming environments, using three representation-learning strategies: observation reconstruction, latent prediction, and redundancy reduction. Curiosity-driven exploration with observation reconstruction yields the strongest aggregate family profile, although the best individual pairing depends on the experiment. In compositional vision-based tasks, intrinsic motivation derived from both episodic and lifelong novelty---providing a complementary memory to the world model's generic recurrent state---

efcbca08087c4fd5170b74c1.title_original: Activation-Guided Graph Retrieval for Cognitive Memory Reconstruction in Language Model Systems
efcbca08087c4fd5170b74c1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented language model systems generally select context by query-conditioned relevance. We argue that long-lived AI systems require a second operator: activation-conditioned memory availability. We specify an architecture in which request and goal cues seed an authorized memory graph, activation and fan attenuation allocate a bounded traversal frontier, retrieved entities recursively emit cues, and a typed evidence graph is reconstructed before generation. The specification yields five architectural consequences about candidate selection, traversal control, graph regularization, evidence reconstruction, and reinforcement. We derive implementation-level cost estimates and define ablations, failure conditions, and a reproducible evaluation protocol. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if a simpler graph reranker matches full traversal on causal and temporal recovery under equal budgets. This architecture-and-analysis preprint reports no benchmark measurements. If the claim holds, retrieval returns the evidence path that makes a memory available, not only a ranked list.

8d5aaf454e34edd09d51f68f.title_original: Agreeing on the Answer but Not the Reason: Measurement Limits of LLM Reasoning Failure Taxonomies
8d5aaf454e34edd09d51f68f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Failure taxonomies for LLM reasoning are increasingly reported as measurements: papers state what fraction of a model's errors fall into named categories, then compare those fractions across models. First, 50.1% of failures carry evidence for more than one category, so the reported plurality depends on the order in which the classifier tests them: reversing two tests moves it in eleven of twelve models, and across all six orderings Collapse's share spans 26.4% to 76.4%. Second, agreement collapses for the category but not for the task. Native speakers of all eleven languages judged 179 transcripts, agreeing with our inspector at kappa = 0.932 on answer correctness but only kappa = 0.093 on Collapse. A second native speaker per language re-rated 142 items; on 121 determinate pairs the two humans agree with each other at kappa = 0.659, while each agrees with the inspector at kappa <= 0.094. Re-running the same inspector model with the human instructions verbatim raises kappa against Human 2 from 0.147 to 0.636, so the gap is largely attributable to the prompt, not the model. 6cf957caeee777b1ace59d9f.title_original: Teaching the Harness: Student-Aware Skill Transfer for LLM Agents
6cf957caeee777b1ace59d9f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13144v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective teaching requires reasoning about the learner as well as the task, a capacity that Theory of Mind describes as inferring another agent's latent state from its behavior. We ask whether a stronger LLM teaches a fixed student better when it applies this principle. The student is an LLM agent acting through a harness that fixes its tools, context, and action budget, so a procedure that helps one model can exhaust the budget of another. We introduce Student-Aware Teaching (SAT). The teacher builds a learner model that pairs an empirical profile with hypotheses about the student's limitations, tests these hypotheses with diagnostic probes, and writes reusable skills for the diagnosed failures. A skill enters the library only after it raises success on matched development tasks. With Claude-Sonnet-5 teaching DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SAT reaches 86.46% task success across four primary runs, leading both a profile-free teacher with the same framework (81.04%) and the untaught student (75.00%) in each run. When DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Gemini-3.8-Flash exchange libraries, each performs better with its own. Saved libraries keep average gains of up to 11.1 points after the teacher leaves. The benefit depends on a student that can follow instructions and a deployment route that del

994d7327a4d607e95d9acca8.title_original: Cognitive Multi-Agent Search and Rescue: Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Collaborative Robotics
994d7327a4d607e95d9acca8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective search and rescue (SAR) operations require autonomous systems capable of coordinating multiple heterogeneous agents, adapting to dynamic hazards, and aligning with human mission intent. Existing language-guided reinforcement learning (RL) methods primarily focus on single-agent instruction following and lack mechanisms for team-level coordination in complex, partially observable environments. This paper presents a Cognitive Multi-Agent Framework based on Language-Grounded Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (LG-HRL) that integrates natural-language understanding, hierarchical policy decomposition, and a shared cognitive workspace to achieve cohesive multi-agent behavior in SAR scenarios. Human instructions are interpreted by a large language model (LLM) and transformed into structured semantic cues that guide high-level strategy selection and role assignment across UAV and UGV agents. A formal Language-Grounded Multi-Agent Hierarchical Decision Process (LG-MAHDP) is introduced to model the interplay between semantic grounding, hierarchical control, and distributed coordination. Comprehensive experiments in a simulated disaster environment show that LG-HRL improves learning speed by 2.3 times, increases coordination coherence by 37%, and enhances subgoal accuracy and hazard avoidance by 46% and 31%, respectively. The system achieves 20-30% higher victim rescue rates, demonstrates emergent role specialization, and adapts

0dc08953057b9321efa7c527.title_original: AI Alignment Is Neither Solvable nor Sufficient
0dc08953057b9321efa7c527.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humans and AI systems increasingly act within the same social and economic environments. Alignment, the goal of ensuring that AI systems act in accordance with human values, is widely regarded as a central challenge for ensuring that AI benefits society while avoiding harm. We argue that this endeavor is misguided. First, alignment is not well defined, as it presumes a sufficiently stable and identifiable set of human intentions or values. Second, where a concrete notion of alignment can be specified, it is not solvable. Third, where alignment appears solvable, solving it would not necessarily mitigate the negative consequences of AI. A key reason is that alignment is typically framed as a property of individual AI systems, while the resulting hybrid societies of humans and machines are complex systems shaped by interactions and feedback loops. Emergent risks, and not only those posed by individual misaligned systems, are therefore likely to become a major source of harm. We conclude that AI safety is an ongoing challenge and not a problem that can be solved once and for all by verifying a particular model property.

3a558879383737530286fdce.title_original: From Process Models to Composable Agentic Workflows: Combining BPMN, Agents and Enterprise Knowledge
3a558879383737530286fdce.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13196v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based agents can reason, use tools and collaborate. However, coordinating increasingly complex agentic applications becomes difficult to understand, monitor and improve. Decisions distributed across prompts, tool calls and application logic make workflows implicit. We introduce **Recursive Capability Composition**, enabling agents to execute business processes and expose them as reusable Agentic Tools. This paper presents a BPMN-based approach to Agentic Workflows, combining explicit orchestration with autonomous reasoning. SemTalk BPMN models are transformed into executable workflows using a LangGraph/Pregel runtime. Agentic Tasks introduce LLM reasoning at selected activities, while conventional BPMN controls process flows, deterministic decisions, system interactions and human approvals. Agentic Participants provide reusable interfaces for agent behavior or other executable processes. BPMN orchestration makes multi-agent systems more understandable and manageable. Explicit process models provide developers and operators with a shared view of workflow structures and execution progress, facilitating debugging, monitoring and optimization. Enterprise agents also need organization-specific context. Process Models and Knowledge Graphs describe activities, participants, information objects, decisions and relationships between processes. They provide structured knowledge of how an organization operates, supporting informed agent

bad44db7c8444aad5c30c557.title_original: Counting Under Disagreement: Dollar-Weighted Measurement, Selective Machine Labelling and Budgeted Human Review from Disagreeing AI Readers of Administrative Text
bad44db7c8444aad5c30c557.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study AI-assisted measurement when one text label applies to many administrative records, the target is a monetary total, and the human readings that anchor the machines disagree. We state exact conditions for a fixed-predictor difference estimator and for a cross-fitted predictor whose folds are assigned to the whole frame before sampling, under Poisson sampling, and assess the implemented fixed-size procedures by simulation: 8 predictors whose own totals span \$11.2-15.0B agree to within \$0.4B once rectified. Two rules that accept machine labels at a stated dollar-weighted error, weighted conformal p-values under a dollar measure and Learn-then-Test on the design estimate of the error, are evaluated on nested held-out folds and on re-draws of the design with synthetic truths; their error control in deployment is not established, and the count-based rule accepts no text under a dollar-drawn sample. In a replay that charges every human label, a two-phase review policy whose calibrator is fitted on its own first phase reduces the RMSE of the total by 28% at a budget of 100 texts relative to dollar-proportional sampling, while pure Neyman allocation fails with an uncalibrated predictor

aa7a591e23dc84cd4f9cb082.title_original: Reliability of Claude Code as an Agentic AI Grading System for Handwritten University Exams
aa7a591e23dc84cd4f9cb082.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study examines the reliability of Claude Code, an agentic deployment of the Claude Opus 4.6 large language model, as a grading system for handwritten university exams. Four research questions addressed agreement with expert human grading on total scores (RQ1), agreement across five question types from multiple choice to evaluative judgement (RQ2), consistency across two independent grading sessions one week apart (RQ3), and the accuracy of AI-generated feedback (RQ4). Claude Code graded the 20-mark mid-term papers of 60 consenting students in a Saudi computer graphics course in a single agentic session, guided by three rubric files. Reliability was estimated on disjoint samples: 20 papers for RQ1, RQ2 and RQ4, and 15 papers for RQ3.
