4ae86f5b23c2c9083aff7c8f.title_ko: JP모건 “미국 휴머노이드 2030년 최대 40만대”…유망 부품사로 로보티즈 지목
4ae86f5b23c2c9083aff7c8f.summary_ko: JP모건은 미국의 휴머노이드 생산량이 2030년 30만~40만대, 2035년 약 150만대에 이를 것으로 전망했다. 초기 투자 기회는 완제품보다 핵심 부품업체에 집중될 것으로 보고 국내 로보티즈 등을 유망 공급업체로 꼽았다. 다만 손·액추에이터·AI와 생산능력이 단기적인 양산 확대를 제약한다고 분석했다.
4ae86f5b23c2c9083aff7c8f.background_ko: JP모건은 인력 부족, 로봇 도입의 경제성 개선, 생산능력 확대가 휴머노이드 시장 성장을 이끌고 있다고 분석했다.

007105a47d78b1b51ee28399.title_original: 소프트뱅크·엔비디아, 연 1만대 생산능력 갖춘 독일 휴머노이드 기업에 6600억 투자
007105a47d78b1b51ee28399.excerpt: 소프트뱅크와 엔비디아가 독일 로봇 기업 애자일 로봇(Agile Robots)에 투자하며 휴머노이드와 피지컬 AI 사업을 강화하고 있다. 이미 산업 현장에 2만개 이상의 로봇 솔루션을 공급한 애자일 로봇은 이번 투자에서 85억달러(약 11조원)의 기업가치를 인정받았으며, 확보한 자금으로 미국 시장 진출과 휴머노이드 생산 확대를 추진할 계획이다.로이터와 블룸버그 등에 따르면 애자일 로봇은 12일(현지시간) 소프트뱅크가 주도한 투자 라운드에서 5억달러(약 6600억원)를 유치했다고 밝혔다. 엔비디아와 일본 히타치, T.캐피털도 참여했다.
007105a47d78b1b51ee28399.summary_ko: 소프트뱅크가 주도하고 엔비디아 등이 참여한 투자에서 독일 애자일 로봇이 5억달러(약 6600억원)를 유치해 기업가치 85억달러를 인정받았다. 투자금은 해외 시장 확대와 제조 역량 강화에 쓰며, 연간 최대 1만대 생산능력을 갖춘 공장에서 올해 휴머노이드 약 2000대 생산을 목표로 한다.
007105a47d78b1b51ee28399.background_ko: 애자일 로봇은 미국 등 해외 시장 진출과 휴머노이드 생산 확대를 추진하고 있으며, 엔비디아와는 이미 로봇 개발 분야에서 협력하고 있다.

d3dc8b1bac15d1af5e5504df.title_original: 아파치 HTTP 서버 2.4.71 공개…HTTP/2 원격 코드 실행 취약점 수정
d3dc8b1bac15d1af5e5504df.excerpt: 아파치 HTTP 서버 프로젝트가 11월 11일 보안 취약점 3건을 수정한 2.4.71을 공개했다. 이 가운데 CVE-2026-119618은 HTTP/2 연결을 처리하는 웹서버에서 외부 공격자가 임의의 코드를 실행할 수 있는 취약점이다. 프로젝트는 이를 ‘치명적’으로 분류했다. 공식 권고에는 실제 악용 사례가 명시되지 않았다. 문제는 HTTP/2 모듈이 여러 요청을 동시에 처리하면서 공유 메모리를 제대로 보호하지 못해 발생한다. 이 과정에서 메모리가 손상되면 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다. 영향 범위는 아파치 HTTP 서버 2.
d3dc8b1bac15d1af5e5504df.title_ko: 아파치 HTTP 서버 2.4.71, HTTP/2 원격 코드 실행 등 취약점 3건 수정
d3dc8b1bac15d1af5e5504df.summary_ko: 아파치 HTTP 서버 2.4.71이 HTTP/2 원격 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-119618 등 보안 결함 3건을 수정했다. 해당 취약점은 서버 2.4.55~2.4.70과 별도 모듈 mod_h2 2.0.8~2.0.42에 영향을 주며, 공식 권고에 실제 악용 사례는 명시되지 않았다. 운영자는 2.4.71 또는 운영체제 배포판의 보안 패키지를 적용해야 한다.
d3dc8b1bac15d1af5e5504df.background_ko: HTTP/2 모듈이 여러 요청을 동시에 처리할 때 공유 메모리를 제대로 보호하지 못해 메모리 손상과 원격 코드 실행으로 이어질 수 있다.

curation.reason_ko: 널리 쓰이는 Apache HTTP 서버의 HTTP/2 원격 코드 실행 결함이 수정돼 업데이트 확인이 중요하다.

612d741dafe0ac4c67b38252.summary_ko: 레일웨이는 10월 20~21일 해킹으로 탈취된 고객 AI 서비스 키의 무단 사용액을 약 74만달러로 추산했다. 복호화된 데이터에 포함된 이용자 1852명의 연동 토큰을 모두 재설정했으며, AI 서비스 제공업체가 환불하지 않는 금액은 자체 부담하겠다고 밝혔다. 초기 발표의 약 10만 워크스페이스는 실제 피해 규모가 아닌 잠재 노출 범위다.

b670a198ddff1cde78060b4c.background_ko: 연구자는 CLFS의 인증 파일 생성 처리와 Windows Defender의 높은 실행 권한을 악용해 공격자가 지정한 위치에 파일을 생성할 수 있다고 설명했다.

curation.reason_ko: Windows SYSTEM 권한 상승 공격 코드가 공개됐으며 시험 보고와 실제 악용 증거 부재를 구분해야 한다.

6a07677e82816612ad173677.excerpt: PHP2Shell enabled initial compromise, while CVE-2026-123039 allowed attackers to elevate privileges to root. The post PHP2Shell Exploited in Destructive Check Point Gateway Attacks appeared first on SecurityWeek .
6a07677e82816612ad173677.title_ko: PHP2Shell 악용한 Check Point 게이트웨이 공격…일부 피해 조직에 와이퍼 배포
6a07677e82816612ad173677.summary_ko: Check Point는 공격자가 PHP2Shell과 권한 상승 취약점을 연계해 게이트웨이에 침투하고, 이스라엘 피해 조직의 VMware ESXi 호스트에 와이퍼를 배포했다고 밝혔다. 10월 30일 시작된 1차 공격과 달리 11월 2일 시작된 다국가 대상 2차 공격에서는 파괴 행위가 관찰되지 않았다. 중국 연계 정황은 있지만 공격 주체는 확정되지 않았다.

This framing misses the errors that matter most. A misread that yields an illegal move is loud. One that yields a legal-but-wrong move is silent, because a legality-only pipeline accepts it and reads every later move against a wrong position. We therefore treat the task as game reconstruction and present Zugwise, which repurposes computer-chess machinery (quiescence search, static exchange evaluation, pin detection) to ask not "what should be played?" but "could a human plausibly have written this?" An absurdity detector makes silent errors loud at or near where they occur, and a backward search traces late symptoms to their cause. Candidate ranking excludes chess-quality signals. A Needleman-Wunsch merge adds the second player's sheet as evidence, and review stops send every disagreement between the sheets' legal readings to a human. In oracle replay of two tournament sections, a release adding them cuts silent errors from 16 to 1 and from 50 to 13. Two learned signals, CTC re-scoring against the recognizer's raw output and a Maia-style human-move prior, raise the correct fix's top-rank rate from 58.8% to 78.0% of the replacement decisions where it is a candidate, and hold without refitting on a later section. 4a255f5021779a8cef31dcb5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents accumulate histories of their own mistakes, and a system that compacts, repairs or hands off such a history decides what it says about those mistakes while their effects stay in the world. Prior work cleans the history at a fixed world, where showing a corrected step and saying it is done move together. We ask whether the same correct content helps or hurts depending on how the history states it and what the world holds. We freeze an agent mid-task with its exact world state, edit the history or the world, and let a receiver model continue. On AgentCE-Bench, after the agent commits a wrong value, we hold the world fixed and add the correct value by two natural edits: a truthful note beside the preserved error or the agent's own completed action. The note raises recovery, the share of remaining targets the receiver gets right, from 51% under a matched neutral note to 66%. The completed action lowers it below the unedited history, from 50% to 44%, so the value's presence alone does not predict the effect. On AppWorld, after a database write, we vary whether its receipt reports success or failure and whether its effect is present. A success receipt lowers whole-task success from 45% to 28% while the effect is absent and raises it from 38% to 49% once present. 139ce156f1deefc05e91cd24.title_original: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
139ce156f1deefc05e91cd24.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14681v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Today's AI workloads are rapidly changing: new models are released more often, model architectures are increasingly diverse, and traffic distributions change frequently. The challenge we face at Together AI is continual optimization for these changing workloads. Compiling a deployment into an optimized forward pass is a challenge that is well-suited for agent hill-climbing. Existing systems struggle with continual compilation due to a tradeoff between measurement throughput and fidelity. Many systems use agents to optimize individual kernels from the inference forward pass using offline benchmarks, but timings are low-fidelity because of data-dependent behavior in primitives like mixture-of-experts (MoE). On the other hand, systems use agents to directly optimize end-to-end engines but suffer from slow engine launch times. To address these challenges, we build Together Compiler (TKCC), the first truly continual agent loop designed for AI inference optimization. To address the throughput-fidelity tradeoff, we propose: (1) a Tiered Persistent Engine that decouples engine launch overheads from forward pass computation; (2) a cost model to select the parallelism configurations that seed the optimization process. We also conduct extensive ablations on agent context management and present our insights on deploying TKCC in production. 46d415b01696e9457eca9285.title_original: When Should Semantic Priors Enter Partially-Identified Causal Discovery?
46d415b01696e9457eca9285.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Observational causal discovery often leaves causal di- rections unresolved or unstable. Large language mod- els (LLMs) can provide semantic information to resolve these directions, but incorrect proposals can exclude the true causal graph and invalidate downstream inference. We study three separate decisions: where to allocate semantic queries, which proposals to admit, and which causal graphs to retain. Our framework distinguishes population non-identifiability from finite-sample insta- bility, evaluates semantic orientation against statistical and random controls, and examines calibrated admis- sion and error-tolerant DAG retention. Experiments across benchmark networks show that semantic infor- mation improves recovery over coin-flip orientations, but targeting unstable edges has no established ad- vantage over matched-random allocation. The tested admission certificate cannot support nontrivial admis- sion with the available calibration tasks. Moreover, downstream retention depends on reference adequacy: learned references contain the true DAG in only three of 80 planned tasks. These findings separate the value of semantic information from the reliability of its alloca- tion, admission, and retention, and identify calibration size and reference adequacy as key limitations.

493576a264e36d019dc094fe.title_original: SynthCorp: A Platform for Creating Benchmarks for Data Agents
493576a264e36d019dc094fe.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Current benchmarks for LLM-driven data agents saturate quickly and cannot target specific capabilities. We present SynthCorp, a platform that creates customizable data estates and benchmarks by simulating how business events produce and modify corporate data over time. Each data estate combines relational databases, a document store, and a data catalog, paired with evaluation tasks and executable gold programs. First, given a scenario and target complexity dimensions, SynthCorp synthesizes reusable event types and compiles each into a program over predefined simulation primitives. Second, SynthCorp schedules event instances on a virtual calendar, interleaving routine and disruption events so that tables, documents, and catalog entries remain consistent. Third, SynthCorp executes the calendar to materialize the data estate and records every operation in a simulation log. Fourth, SynthCorp generates analytical tasks and derives verified gold programs from the log. We use SynthCorp to generate initial evaluation benchmarks comprising seven data estates (up to 1K operational tables) and 256 tasks across five domains. The data estates pass deterministic pipeline checks (such as foreign-key violations, undeclared writes, recurrence violations, and database execution failures) with a near-zero error rate, introduce cross-asset complexities, and cover all requested dimensions. 60225d297d2baf61a82bad8c.title_original: Rational Use of Time for Social Coordination in Humans and AI
60225d297d2baf61a82bad8c.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: All social interactions are situated in time. Previous studies have shown that humans are able to use implicit temporal cues, such as the duration of a pause, to infer others' mental states. But how do humans use temporal cues for dynamic, fine-grained social coordination? And can AI systems do the same, without ``experiencing'' continuous real-time as humans do? We study these questions using a cooperative card game task called The Mind, which requires players to achieve a shared goal across repeated interactions but forbids explicit communication: the only available signal is the passage of time. We evaluate 150 humans, and two classes of AI models which reflect different ways of operationalizing time in artificial systems: computer-use agents (CUAs), and standard text-prompted LLMs. We find that human behavior is best captured by a Bayesian strategy that infers a partner's belief from their timing---and similarly for frontier models. However, unlike humans, none of the tested models seem to efficiently adapt their behaviors to their partners' over the course of the game. From a cognitive perspective, our findings suggest that humans perform implicit probabilistic reasoning about continuous-time signals in dynamic social settings, and that such reasoning mechanisms may emerge without real-time experience. 79609066248896fee8a9c37d.title_original: Leaderboard Hacking: Preference-Based Model Evaluations are Vulnerable to Manipulation
79609066248896fee8a9c37d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14769v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Arena-style rankings of language models are a widely used evaluation framework in online leaderboards, research papers, and model evaluation in production. These rankings aim to realistically assess model performance using pairwise comparisons of anonymous models on user prompts, aggregating votes via the Bradley-Terry model to produce the final ranking. However, we find that these leaderboards are highly vulnerable to several manipulation strategies that unscrupulous providers could use to boost a model's rank: strategic voting (individual votes that boost a model's rank, including votes on irrelevant models), strategic prompting (choosing prompts that favor a model), and strategic nomination (boosting the rank of a model by inserting irrelevant models). We demonstrate these effects on public leaderboard data, analyze the circumstances that cause these vulnerabilities, and describe approaches to safeguard against each attack. Notably, these issues hold for any preference-based evaluation using the Bradley-Terry model that allows open prompting, voting, or model submission. These manipulations boost the rank of nearly every tested model; each attack can boost a model by up to 15-20 places in a ranking and, combined, they can boost a model by up to 45 places.

3b819e87762292f3a7f596d0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that perform state estimation using pretrained perception models, e.g., Vision-Language Models (VLMs), face the fundamental challenge that predictions are uncertain. Still, most approaches determinize these predictions into a single best-guess state and make decisions as if it were ground truth. This is brittle because when the guess is wrong, the agent's decisions may be unsafe or infeasible. At the other extreme, maintaining a full probability distribution over symbolic states is often intractable. We propose a middle path, drawing on the underlying probabilities the perception model already produces (e.g., a VLM's output-layer token distributions) to construct a $\theta$-confidence Minimal Belief Set (MBS$_\theta$), a minimal subset of states whose cumulative probability meets a user-specified belief-mass threshold. The minimality of an MBS$_\theta$ ensures that the agent considers only the most likely states, enhancing robustness in downstream decision-making while maintaining computational tractability. Using a novel three-layered belief system, we efficiently approximate individual state probabilities from per-feature predictions and task-level constraints. On this belief construction, we base our MBS$_\theta$ construction, while maintaining only a lean factored representation of the belief. 57a85161c8497737b265e073.title_original: When Is Proof-Step Verification Worth Its Cost? Operating Requirements of Certify-or-Decline Verification for Open-Weight Mathematical Reasoning
57a85161c8497737b265e073.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-step verification rewrites a solver's answer into typed steps and uses LLM judges to certify or decline. We evaluate this pipeline on open-weight models across GPQA, AIME-2025, and a MATH-500 subset. Certification raises answer-key-match precision by 31 percentage points on the strong GPQA configuration and 46 on AIME, while answering only 35% and 21% of attempts. On near-ceiling MATH-500, gains are at most 5 points at a loss of 13-27 points of coverage. An output-token-matched self-consistency selector obtains 82.9% precision at 35% coverage, compared with the verifier's pooled 87.6% (paired difference: +4.8 points, 95% interval [-8.2, 18.5]). A diagnostic sample reveals a distinct failure mode: 52 of 88 completed problems end in invalid proof construction without ever reaching a judge. Finally, external-LLM acceptance of rendered certified chains is 61.0-67.6%, compared with 87.6% answer-key match. These audits lack human or formal-kernel ground truth. Open-weight auditor pairs show near-zero chance-corrected agreement, which measures consistency rather than accuracy against proof truth. These results motivate separate reporting of execution failures, selected-answer precision, and independently assessed proof validity. We provide per-configuration results and evaluation details in the supplement.

The context contains evaluated designs labeled desired (Class 1) or undesired (Class 0). f8511a052786b35056380766.title_original: AutoAssumption: Searching over Assumptions Discovers ML-Systems Algorithms
f8511a052786b35056380766.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14844v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many advances in ML systems came from breaking an assumption that earlier methods took for granted: speculative decoding dropped the assumption that a model needs one forward pass per token. cbb9f04d79a769394210cda8.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI systems increasingly undertake extended tasks and act on people's behalf, making human-agent interaction central to their effectiveness. This paper examines how foundations developed by the Autonomous Agents and Multi-Agent Systems (AAMAS) community inform these demands. We consider interactions ranging from individual human-agent partnerships to teams and larger groups, where participants differ in their roles, decision authority, capabilities, and objectives. We organize computational approaches around the connected challenges of understanding others and deciding how to interact with them. Theory of Mind, belief-desire-intention architectures, goal and plan recognition, inverse planning, and recursive reasoning provide mechanisms for representing and inferring partially observable mental states. Observer-aware planning, model reconciliation, and decision-theoretic communication connect these inferences to action, explanation, and information exchange. Together with shared autonomy, argumentation, and cooperative inverse reinforcement learning, these approaches offer foundations for agentic systems that account for evolving human knowledge, intentions, and expectations. 31d5716a9a820a9984ebee0f.title_original: Effective Teacher Support for Reasoning Distillation
31d5716a9a820a9984ebee0f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Forward-KL language-model distillation normally computes dense teacher and student scores over the full vocabulary at every supervised position, making training and stored teacher targets expensive. We instead distill from the teacher's highest-probability vocabulary fraction, renormalizing the retained mass as we sweep support from 100% to 0.01%. Our main study distills Qwen3 4B -> 1.7B. We confirm the broader support-reduction finding on larger Qwen3 8B -> 4B and Nemotron Nano 12B -> 9B pairs and under answer-only supervision. We evaluate generation primarily on MMLU-Pro and secondarily on GPQA-Diamond. Across the Qwen3 settings, retaining 0.01% of the vocabulary causes no observed MMLU-Pro degradation relative to full-vocabulary distillation, although disagreement with the complete teacher distribution increases. Nemotron Nano matches full-vocabulary MMLU-Pro at 0.1%, but smaller fractions fail to emit the closing reasoning tag, showing that the reliable cutoff depends on the model family. At 0.01% support, caching the retained next-token scores from the teacher forward pass cuts training step time by 38%, while restricting student output computation to those tokens cuts peak memory by 24%; neither causes observed MMLU-Pro degradation.

de0acd39ac0ccf37b38c8fc1.title_original: Can an AI Agent Be Epistemically Akratic? Higher-Order Evidence & the Limits of Self-Correction
de0acd39ac0ccf37b38c8fc1.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When we judge that our reasoning was defective, it seems plausible that we should abandon the conclusion it produced. This thought has special force for AI agents built to assess and correct their own work. Yet obeying such judgments can make an agent worse at distinguishing sound reasoning from defective reasoning. An AI agent may rely on information about its reasoning when deciding which conclusions to keep, while the part that judges whether those conclusions are justified cannot use that information. The agent can then exercise an epistemic competence by retaining conclusions it judges unjustified, even when its self-assessments are generally reliable. Nor is the difficulty resolved by training the agent to make its conclusions and assessments agree: agreement can be achieved by degrading either one. Crucially, I argue that a negative assessment can remain valuable by identifying conclusions requiring further scrutiny, without having authority to eliminate them. The result challenges a central assumption about AI self-correction: that bringing an agent's beliefs into agreement with its own self-assessment about their justification makes it better at correcting its mistakes.

c410404db383d4700898321f.title_original: MuEdit: An efficient multi-task editing method towards inter-domain knowledge conflicts
c410404db383d4700898321f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) require frequent knowledge updates across heterogeneous domains, but existing editing methods fail when applied sequentially to multi-task settings. We trace this collapse to inter-domain null-space misalignment: heterogeneous tasks induce distinct Jacobian geometries, causing their common null space to shrink dramatically and leaving insufficient admissible directions for conflict-free updates. We propose the Conflict Index to quantify this geometric interference, and introduce Mu-Edit, which mitigates multi-task conflicts via (1) conflict-aware ordering to minimize cumulative interference, and (2) dynamic low-rank approximation to expand the null space when ordering alone is insufficient. Experiments across five functional domains and three backbones show that Mu-Edit significantly outperforms existing baselines in multi-task editing performance while preserving general capabilities, and remains effective under incremental task arrival.

9ce159f8ceca663cb468c48d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deployment of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for Edge-AI is constrained by memory and bandwidth limitations. A standard 7B parameter model consumes 14 GB Video Random Access Memory (VRAM) in half-precision (FP16), precluding co-location of vector indices and Key-Value (KV) caches. Our system-level analysis identifies a critical trade-off: while generative pre-trained transformer quantization (GPTQ) offers superior throughput (51.6 tok/s), it exhibits significant context instability at 2048+ tokens on Turing architectures. Conversely, NormalFloat 4-bit (NF4) maintains robust long-context performance with viable latency (81 ms/tok). By coupling NF4 with a decoupled Florence-2 vision integration, we achieve visual reasoning with only 430 MB VRAM overhead. Furthermore, empirical observations of prompt-induced search space pruning show that structured prompting reduces latency by 47% without altering computational intensity (1.88 GFLOPs/token). The integrated architecture maintains an 8.37 GB footprint, establishing a viable RAG pipeline for 12-16 GB GPUs. Finally, structured few-shot prompting effectively compensates for quantization-induced reasoning loss, restoring mathematical accuracy from 35.0% to 92.0% across 200 trials.

400e561c7974f25f0eafea2a.title_original: Emergent Vision-Shaped Thinking in Text-Only Reasoning through Multimodal Training
400e561c7974f25f0eafea2a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14942v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does multimodal training shape how a language model thinks, even when the input is text only? We test this with targeted causal ablations across 10 multimodal configurations from 6 model families, with matched text-only backbones and cross-family transfer controls. We contrast spatial-imagery tasks that invite mental scene construction with symbol-manipulation tasks solvable by symbolic rules alone. We identify a vision-language axis in hidden-state space and ablate its projection at inference. In Chameleon-7B, this ablation drops accuracy on BIG-Bench Hard (BBH) navigate by 27.6 pp while leaving boolean expressions intact (+5.6 pp), a 33.2 pp double dissociation. The effect is direction-specific and layer-localized, extends to mental-simulation tasks such as mental rotation, paper folding, and perspective taking, and is not explained by task difficulty, reasoning depth, or sequential update load. Together, these results reveal emergent vision-shaped thinking (EVT): text-only reasoning that causally recruits representations introduced or strengthened by vision-language training, without assuming an image-like internal format. The measured effect is spatially concentrated at 7-8B and broadens to non-spatial visual attribute binding in the tested 32B configuration. In dual-path unified models (BAGEL, Janus-Pro), the causal handle localizes to the generation pathway as a compact one-dimensional carrier. The understanding pathway al

61f93787485a183bbc5563c7.title_original: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
61f93787485a183bbc5563c7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14949v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce \bench{}, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distribution generalization to unseen equation templates and shifted coefficient ranges. We further introduce RSI-PDE, a recursively self-improving agent harness that shortlists candidate equations by residual loss, uses relative $L^2$ feedback to refine coefficients and numerical solvers, and applies a validation gate to policy and memory updates. We compare RSI-PDE with single-run baselines and native agent harnesses (Claude Code or Codex) across four frontier models. Across the three settings, RSI-PDE improves the pass rate averaged across the four models by 106.5--181.9\% relative to single-run baselines and by 3.0--19.6\% relative to native harnesses, while reducing total recorded model calls by 46.9\% ac

cea72db4bd8e768f61df9dc9.title_original: Termination Lag: Coding Agents Solve Early but Stop Late
cea72db4bd8e768f61df9dc9.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Coding agents can solve a task well before they stop working on it. We characterize \emph{termination lag}--the number of steps between an agent's first correct patch and the end of its run--across five models, two agent frameworks, and three SWE-bench datasets by recording and testing every distinct repository patch generated during execution. Our analysis reveals that 38--82% of successful runs achieve a correct solution on their initial source-code edit. However, agents continue to expend substantial effort after correct patches, with post-solution steps accounting for a median of 35--37% for Qwen3-Coder and 54--60% for Laguna-XS.2 in successful runs on SWE-bench Verified and Multilingual. Agents spend most of these additional steps verifying their work and exploring the repository. In a small fraction of cases (1--8%), this continued activity leads agents to undo their earlier correct patch, leaving the final solution incorrect.
cea72db4bd8e768f61df9dc9.title_ko: 코딩 에이전트, 정답을 만든 뒤에도 작업 계속…종료 지연 분석

4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.title_original: Early Signals, Strong Decisions: Prefix-Guided Sampling for Parallel Test-Time Scaling
4ce6bb44c1571ab30124b140.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parallel test-time scaling (TTS) has been shown to enhance reasoning in large language models by generating and aggregating multiple independent reasoning paths. Internal confidence scores can further improve this process by identifying paths of varying quality. However, existing methods remain computationally inefficient, as low-quality paths are fully expanded before being evaluated. In this work, we aim to improve the use of internal confidence signals for better model performance and computational efficiency. We begin by offering a new perspective on the role of confidence in aggregation, showing that it is most impactful for questions near the decision boundary. Notably, when amplified by multi-sample aggregation, even small confidence signals derived from short prefixes can meaningfully influence outcomes in these boundary cases. Building on this insight, we introduce Prefix-Guided Sampling (PreG), a method that reallocates computation by first generating short prefixes, ranking them using internal confidence scores, and then completing only the most promising candidates. This strategy reduces token usage while maintaining gains in path quality. We provide theoretical analysis demonstrating that, under a fixed compute budget, PreG strengthens the effective signal by widening the decision boundary margin. Empirically, our method consistently outperforms standard parallel TTS approaches across benchmarks, while significantly

c1b2a9694f8b13efc30036d2.title_original: Same Task, Different Statement: When and How Reformulation Helps LLM Problem Solving
c1b2a9694f8b13efc30036d2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.14997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When people face a hard problem, they often restate it in a clearer way before solving it. We study whether the same habit helps large language models by rewriting the statement of a problem. A legal rewrite must keep the meaning, the constraints, and the correct answer unchanged. We test three kinds of rewrites. Decomposition makes hidden subgoals explicit. Typed Reformulation casts the task into a more suitable solving frame. Concept Reduction removes surface detail and exposes the task structure. We evaluate them on eight math, logic, and code benchmarks with eight models, all under the same chain-of-thought solving prompt. The effect is large but depends on the problem type. An oracle that picks the best rewrite after the fact raises accuracy by +27.6% on average. Yet no single rewrite helps every problem, and a mismatched rewrite can hurt. Still, the effect follows clear patterns. Each kind of rewrite fits certain problem types. A simple fixed rule learned from one set of problems transfers part of the gain to new problems. It gains +11.0% on the problems it chooses to rewrite, while blind rewriting loses 5.6% on a similar share of problems. Rewriting is therefore not a universal way to solve problems. The question is when and how to rewrite.

378c4a8d6aff8016781bea41.title_original: EvoX: Rethinking the Agent Harness as a Runtime Policy
378c4a8d6aff8016781bea41.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly interact with tools and environments, yet plausible model decisions do not always translate into successful execution due to tool-call mismatches, interrupted workflows, and unsupported completion claims. We present EvoX, a Rust-based, multi-model agent runtime guided by The Second Policy, which views the harness as an Operational Policy complementing the foundation model's Semantic Policy. EvoX combines model-facing guidance with deterministic runtime control through three complementary mechanisms: Action Realization, Execution Continuity, and Outcome Grounding. To evaluate harnesses without suppressing their native behaviors, we introduce Contrast, a controlled and auditable framework integrating explicit fairness constraints, provider-bound request verification, and evidence-based adjudication. Across five benchmarks, six foundation models, and six agent harnesses, EvoX achieves the highest numerical success rate of 56.2% over 691 common task--model pairs, exceeding the average of the other five harnesses by approximately 3.0 percentage points. Its larger advantages on GLM-5.3 (+10.7 points) and Kimi K3 (+7.9 points) highlight the model-dependent effectiveness of harness design and the potential for cross-provider adaptability. Achieved without memory, evolution, or extensions, these results establish EvoX as a competitive multi-model agent runtime and underscore the importance o

e7201364c8d75ea1e1c59fbf.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Humanity has long sought to explain natural phenomena. Reliable prediction of experimental outcomes is a central test of our understanding of the processes that produce them. If artificial general intelligence (AGI) is to surpass human scientific capabilities, it must also predict experimental outcomes more reliably than humans. Such capabilities could accelerate scientific discovery across disciplines, help address humanity's most pressing challenges, and improve human well-being. We introduce Science Prediction Universe (SPU), a benchmark of hidden experimental outcomes with 100 public verified tasks from chemistry, materials science, biology and medicine, and 16 private tasks from unpublished wet-lab experiments. Given an experimental setup and candidate conditions, an agent works with any resources it needs to rank the candidates by a measured outcome. We evaluate thirteen agent configurations spanning twelve frontier models across two harnesses (Codex and Claude Code). Current agents remain far from saturating wet-lab outcome prediction, with substantial performance disparities across models: on the public benchmark, configurations separate into two distinct tiers, with task-adjusted Spearman correlations ranging from 0.227 for the lowest-performing configuration to 0.478 for the best. Analysis of 1,155 scored public trajectories (227,103 tool calls) suggests that the bottleneck lies in scientific judgment rather than tool
e7201364c8d75ea1e1c59fbf.title_ko: SPU, AI 에이전트의 과학 실험 결과 예측 능력 평가
e7201364c8d75ea1e1c59fbf.summary_ko: 연구진은 화학·재료과학·생물학·의학의 검증된 공개 과제 100개와 미발표 실험 기반 비공개 과제 16개로 구성한 SPU를 제안했다. 최신 모델 12개를 활용한 에이전트 구성 13종을 평가했으며, 공개 과제의 과제별 조정 스피어먼 상관계수는 0.227~0.478로 구성 간 성능 차이가 컸다고 보고했다.
e7201364c8d75ea1e1c59fbf.background_ko: 연구진은 실험 결과의 신뢰성 있는 예측을 과학적 이해의 핵심 검증 기준으로 보고, 인간을 넘어서는 AI의 과학 역량을 평가하고자 했다.

e192d124f5a5f31c5720b306.title_original: Advancing Weighted Partial MaxSAT Solving via Differentiable GPU Guidance
e192d124f5a5f31c5720b306.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15091v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a GPU-CPU hybrid framework for Weighted Partial MaxSAT (WPMAX-SAT) that complements state-of-the-art CPU solvers with differentiable GPU optimization. The GPU stage directly optimizes instance-specific categorical decision parameters without a training dataset or a pretrained predictive model. The central challenge in extending differentiable optimization to WPMAX-SAT is the hard/soft clause asymmetry: hard clauses represent inviolable feasibility constraints while soft clauses carry weights. We introduce a hierarchical differentiable loss that prioritizes hard clause satisfaction before optimizing the weighted soft objective, ensuring that GPU gradient descent leans towards the constraint structure of WPMAX-SAT. Our framework transforms the GPU-optimized variable logits to high-confidence assignments and transfers them to CPU solvers via two complementary modes: partial guidance, which injects the most confident perturbed partial variable assignments as soft clauses into $N$ parallel solver instances, and phase initialization, which guides the CDCL solver's internal branching polarity with the full GPU assignment as a warm start to preserve the problem's originality. We evaluate on all 229 instances of the MSE 2024 (most recent due to cancellation in 2025) anytime weighted benchmark with the top 2 winners as baselines; our hybrid framework improves the average solution score by up to 4.9% over tt-open-wbo-inc-Glucose

a648f9673761c39640ddd089.title_original: A frontier machine intelligence for human neuroimaging
a648f9673761c39640ddd089.excerpt: arXiv:2611.15094v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical imaging is essential for diagnosing disease, guiding treatment and monitoring patients over time. Although artificial intelligence has advanced image interpretation, existing medical models often address restricted tasks, while general-purpose proprietary models lack access to private clinical imaging required to achieve medical expertise. Developing models that can interpret complex examinations and communicate their findings in the context of clinical decisions remains a major challenge. Here, we show that Neuro-VL, a vision-language model trained on nearly one million neuroimaging studies from routine clinical care, can interpret complete imaging examinations and engage in natural language conversations about their findings. Across internal and international datasets, Neuro-VL outperformed frontier general-purpose and specialized medical models in diagnosing, localizing, and describing abnormalities, as well as generating comprehensive radiology reports. The model also compared serial examinations to assess disease progression and more reliably resisted misleading clinical assumptions than leading frontier models from OpenAI and Google. These results extend health system learning beyond individual predictions to interactive image interpretation and longitudinal disease monitoring. They demonstrate how the collective clinical experience of health systems can be used to develop medical AI with specialized expertise and
a648f9673761c39640ddd089.title_ko: 뇌영상 검사 약 100만 건으로 학습한 Neuro-VL, 영상 해석·질병 추적 연구
a648f9673761c39640ddd089.summary_ko: 연구진은 일상 진료의 뇌영상 검사 약 100만 건으로 학습한 시각언어 모델 Neuro-VL을 제시했다. 내부·국제 데이터 평가에서 이상 소견의 진단·위치 파악·설명과 영상의학 보고서 작성이 비교 모델보다 우수했다고 보고했다. 연속 검사 비교를 통한 질병 진행 평가와 검사 결과에 관한 자연어 대화도 수행했다.
